name: Deep Learning
description: Designing and training neural networks, including CNNs, sequence models and transformers, with frameworks such as PyTorch.

resources.title: Kaggle Learn: Intro to Deep Learning

questions.question: Why are non-linear activation functions such as ReLU used between layers of a neural network?
options: To reduce the number of parameters
Without them, stacked linear layers collapse into a single linear function and cannot model non-linear patterns
To normalize the input data
To make training deterministic
questions.explanation: A composition of linear maps is linear; non-linearities let deep networks represent complex functions.

questions.question: What does one epoch mean during training?
options: One forward pass of a single example
One update of the learning rate
One complete pass through the entire training dataset
One layer of the network
questions.explanation: An epoch is one full pass over all training examples, typically made of many mini-batch steps.

questions.question: Why are convolutional layers well suited to image data?
options: They share weights across spatial positions and exploit local patterns, needing far fewer parameters than fully connected layers
They convert images to grayscale automatically
They do not require any training
They process each pixel independently of its neighbors
questions.explanation: Convolutions apply the same small filters across the image, capturing local features with translation equivariance and parameter sharing.

questions.question: In a PyTorch training loop, why is optimizer.zero_grad() called each iteration?
options: To reset the model weights to zero
To set the learning rate to zero
To disable gradient tracking during evaluation
Because gradients accumulate by default in .grad, so they must be cleared before the next backward pass
questions.explanation: loss.backward() adds to existing .grad values; without zeroing, gradients from previous batches would be summed in.

questions.question: What problem do residual (skip) connections, as in ResNet, primarily help with?
options: Reducing the size of the training dataset
Making very deep networks easier to optimize by improving gradient flow
Removing the need for activation functions
Guaranteeing zero training loss
questions.explanation: Skip connections give gradients a direct path backwards, mitigating degradation and vanishing gradients in deep networks.

questions.question: In scaled dot-product attention, why are the scores QK^T divided by sqrt(d_k)?
options: To convert the scores into probabilities
To reduce memory usage
To make the attention matrix symmetric
To keep dot products from growing large with dimension, which would push softmax into regions with tiny gradients
questions.explanation: Large dot products saturate softmax; scaling by sqrt(d_k) keeps variance stable and gradients useful.

practical.title: Write a PyTorch training step
practical.instructions: Given a PyTorch model, an optimizer, a loss function criterion, and a batch (inputs, targets), write the lines of code for one training step: compute predictions, compute the loss, clear old gradients, backpropagate and update the weights.
practical.expected_output: outputs = model(inputs); loss = criterion(outputs, targets); optimizer.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); optimizer.step()

rubric.description: Runs a forward pass and computes the loss

rubric.hint: Call optimizer.zero_grad() so gradients from earlier batches do not accumulate.
Call optimizer.step() to apply the gradient update.

tasks.title: Learn neural network fundamentals
tasks.description: Complete the Kaggle Intro to Deep Learning course, covering neurons, activation functions, stochastic gradient descent, overfitting and dropout.

tasks.title: Train an image classifier with PyTorch
tasks.description: Follow the PyTorch beginner tutorial to train a small network on FashionMNIST. Write the training and evaluation loops yourself and track loss per epoch.
tasks.completion_criteria: Model reaches at least 85% test accuracy with a loss curve plotted.

tasks.title: Fine-tune a pretrained CNN
tasks.description: Use transfer learning to fine-tune a pretrained ResNet on a small custom image dataset. Apply data augmentation and compare training from scratch versus fine-tuning.
tasks.completion_criteria: Comparison table showing fine-tuning outperforms training from scratch, with augmentation used.

tasks.title: Build and analyze a transformer-based model
tasks.description: Implement or fine-tune a small transformer for a text classification task. Run experiments on learning rate and model size, and visualize attention or errors to explain model behavior.
tasks.completion_criteria: Repository with training code, experiment log of at least 3 runs and a written analysis.
